items.text: Humans have caused the extinction of species like the great auk and pushed many others, such as orangutans and hedgehogs, to the brink . The great auk, a flightless seabird, was hunted for food, feathers, and oil, disappearing completely in 1844. This tragedy helped scientists realize that human actions can drive species to extinction. Today, deforestation, pollution, and climate change are causing a sixth mass extinction. Over a million species are at risk, with entire ecosystems collapsing. The humble hedgehog, for example, is disappearing due to urban expansion, pesticides , and habitat loss. In 2022, countries pledged to protect 30% of the planet by 2030. Individuals like Hotlin Ompusunggu, an Indonesian dentist, have also made a difference. She offers low-cost treatment to those who protect forests, which helps save orangutans. To prevent mass extinction, governments, businesses, and individuals must work together. Difficult words: brink (the edge), pesticide (a substance used for destroying insects or other organisms harmful to cultivated plants or animals), habitat (the natural home or environment of an animal or plant). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many animals are dying out because of people, like the great auk. Others, such as orangutans and hedgehogs, are in danger. The great auk was a bird. People hunted auks for food and feathers before it died out in 1844. This event showed that human actions can cause extinctions . Today, cutting down trees, dirty water and land, and climate change are hurting animals and plants. More than a million species are in danger. Hedgehogs are disappearing because cities are expanding, and people are using chemicals which kill hedgehogs. In 2022, countries promised to protect 30% of nature by 2030. Some people, like Indonesian dentist Hotlin Ompusunggu, are also helping. Those who protect forests and save orangutans get cheaper care. To stop extinctions, we all need to do something now. Difficult words: feathers (soft and light things that cover a bird’s body), extinction (when animals or plants are gone forever), species (a group of animals or plants). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Humans make some animals go extinct , like the great auk. Other animals, like orangutans and hedgehogs, are in danger . The great auk is a bird which cannot fly. People hunt it too much. The last one dies in 1844. There are no more auks. Today, cutting down forests, using too many chemicals, and climate change are hurting animals. Many animals and plants may die out. Hedgehogs are in trouble because cities are growing, and people are destroying their homes. In 2022, countries promise to protect nature. Some people, like Hotlin Ompusunggu, a dentist from Indonesia, are helping too. She gives cheap care to people who save trees. If we all work together, we can save animals and plants. Difficult words: extinct (gone forever), in danger (in a situation where you may get hurt or die), protect (to keep safe).

In 2015, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau promised to improve Canada’s relationship with Indigenous people and reduce their high imprisonment rates. However, the situation has worsened. Indigenous people, who make up only 5% of Canada’s population, now represent over a third of those under strict supervision after prison. Marvin Starblanket, an Indigenous man from Saskatoon, has spent much of his life in prison due to violent crimes. Currently, he is under a five-year supervision order, restricting his movements, housing, and employment. These orders, meant for rare cases, disproportionately affect Indigenous people. Many face parole denials and strict conditions, increasing their incarceration rates. The causes include poverty, trauma, and lack of opportunities. While some believe supervision provides support, others argue it limits freedom. Starblanket now focuses on his family and hopes to study psychology and advocate for Indigenous rights after his order ends in 2027. He fears the challenge of adjusting to true independence. Difficult words: disproportionately (too much or too little compared to others), parole (early release from prison), incarceration (imprisonment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2015, Prime Minister Trudeau promised to help Indigenous people and lower their high prison numbers. But the problem is even worse. Indigenous people are only 5% of Canada’s population but are more than a third of those under strict rules after prison. Marvin Starblanket, from Saskatoon, spent years in prison for violent crimes. Now he is under a five-year supervision order , which controls where he lives and works. Many Indigenous people face these orders, which makes it harder for them to be free. Many of these people are poor, and they have bad past experiences. Some say supervision helps, but others feel it takes away freedom . Starblanket wants to go to university and help Indigenous people in the future. Difficult words: violent (hurting people), supervision order (when the court controls someone’s actions), freedom (being free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2015, Prime Minister Trudeau promises to help Canada’s Indigenous people. He wants to stop so many from going to prison. But now, the problem is worse. Indigenous people are a small part of Canada’s population. But many are in prison or under rules after leaving. Marvin Starblanket is an Indigenous man. He stays in prison for many years. Now, he has a five-year rule which controls where he lives and works. Many Indigenous people have the same problem. They are poor or go through difficult things. Some think that these rules help. Others say they take away freedom . Starblanket wants to study and help Indigenous people in the future. Difficult words: Indigenous (people who live in a place for a long time), rule (what you must do), freedom (when you are free to do what you want). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bhutan has begun constructing a new city near the Indian border to boost its economy and stop the increasing loss of skilled workers. The Prime Minister believes this project could raise Bhutan’s population to three million. The city, named Galu Mindfulness City (GMC), is being built on 25,000 square kilometers of land as a special administrative region. Bhutan aims to create an eco-friendly and safe city, attracting only selected investors. Essential infrastructure is being upgraded, including border crossings, while India is working on a cross-border railway to improve access. The city will focus on sustainability, using hydroelectric power and traditional Bhutanese values. The project is expected to take 21 years, and its vision is based on happiness, well-being, and mindfulness. Many Bhutanese hope GMC will bring prosperity , better roads, and an international airport, significantly improving their country’s economy. The government remains committed to maintaining its cultural values while promoting growth. Difficult words: boost (to help or encourage something to increase or improve), essential (necessary), prosperity (success and wealth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Bhutan is building a new city on its border with India to help its economy and stop skilled people from leaving. The Prime Minister says this could increase Bhutan’s population to three million. The city called Galu Mindfulness City (GMC) will be eco-friendly , safe, and modern. The government will allow only some companies to take part in the project. The government is improving roads and border crossings, and India is helping by building a railway to Bhutan. The city will use hydroelectric power and follow Bhutanese traditions of happiness and mindfulness. It will take 21 years to finish. Many people believe GMC will make Bhutan richer, bring better roads, and create jobs. The government wants to grow the economy but keep its culture strong. Difficult words: skilled (able to do some things), eco-friendly (not harmful to the natural world), hydroelectric power (using water to make electricity). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bhutan is building a new city near India. The government wants to help the economy . Skilled people are leaving Bhutan. The government wants people to stay. The city is called Galu Mindfulness City (GMC). It will be clean, safe, and modern. Only some companies can invest in it. The government is making roads better. India is helping by building a train line to Bhutan. The city will use water power for electricity. It will take 21 years to finish. People hope it will bring jobs, better roads, and more money. Bhutan wants to grow but keep its culture. Difficult words: economy (money and business of a country), skilled (good at something), invest (to give money to a business). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new world record for the largest polar bear dip was set in the Czech Republic on March 1, 2025. A total of 2,461 swimmers braved the icy waters of Most Lake to beat the previous record of 1,799 participants, set in Poland in 2015. According to Guinness World Records, participants must wear bathing suits, submerge at least to their waists, and remain in the water for at least one minute. Additionally, the water temperature must be below 10°C. On the day of the event, the temperature was a freezing 3.5°C. This extreme winter tradition attracted global attention as people celebrated the achievement and the courage of those involved. The participants were cold and wet but excited to be part of history. Events like this show how people enjoy testing their limits and coming together for unique challenges. Given the success of this event, it is likely that other countries will attempt to break the record in the future. Difficult words: brave (to endure or face unpleasant conditions or behavior without showing fear), submerge (to go under the water). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On March 1, 2025, 2,461 people in the Czech Republic broke the world record for the biggest polar bear dip. They jumped into the freezing water of Most Lake to beat the old record of 1,799 swimmers from Poland in 2015. To set the record, people had to wear swimsuits, go into the water at least to their waists , and stay there for one minute. The water had to be colder than 10°C, and on this day, it was only 3.5°C. This event was very exciting, and many people around the world watched it. The swimmers were cold but happy. People love testing themselves in difficult situations, and another country will likely try to break this record in the future. Difficult words: waist (the part of the body between the ribs and the hips), likely (probably).

On March 1, 2025, many people swim in cold water in the Czech Republic. There are 2,461 swimmers. This is the biggest polar bear dip ever. Before this, the record is 1,799 people in Poland. This record is from 2015. To make a record, people must wear swimsuits, go into the water up to their waist , and stay for one minute. The water must be very cold. On this day, it is only 3.5°C! People around the world watch this big event . The swimmers are cold but happy. Many people like to do difficult things for fun. Maybe another group will try to make a new record later. Difficult words: polar bear dip (an outdoor swim in winter, often through ice), waist (the part of the body between the legs and chest), event (a thing which happens or takes place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Kenya, an invisible workforce is raising concerns. These workers spend long hours reviewing massive amounts of data to improve artificial intelligence (AI) systems. Their role is crucial, however, they earn much less than their counterparts in wealthier countries. Many say the work is mentally exhausting, leaving them traumatized and distressed . Joanne, a data annotator, describes labeling images and categorizing disturbing content, such as explicit photos and violent scenes. Another worker, Stacy, moderates videos on TikTok, often seeing graphic content like accidents or violent crimes. Exposure to such material affects their mental health, leading to anxiety and nightmares. While some companies provide minimal psychological support, it is often inadequate . Experts argue that tech companies outsourcing these tasks to developing countries must ensure fair wages and better working conditions. Workers are starting to unite through associations to demand rights and protections. Without proper intervention, the AI industry risks exploiting vulnerable workers for profit. Difficult words: counterpart (a person or thing that has the same position or purpose as another person or thing in a different place or organization), distressed (suffering from extreme anxiety or pain), inadequate (not enough or good enough). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Kenya, workers are speaking out about their difficult jobs. They spend long hours checking and sorting online content to help improve artificial intelligence (AI) systems. But they earn very little and say the work is emotionally hard. Joanne explains that she labeled images and videos, including violent and upsetting content. Stacy, another worker, checked TikTok videos and saw scenes such as accidents and crimes. Many workers feel stressed and have nightmares. Some companies offer therapy, but it is not enough. Experts say AI companies should pay workers fairly and provide better conditions. Workers are now forming groups to fight for their rights. If nothing changes, more workers will have problems while big companies make a lot of money. Difficult words: speak out (to say openly what you think), earn (to make money), violent (using force to hurt or attack). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Kenya, people work long hours to help artificial intelligence (AI) learn. They look at many pictures and videos and sort them into groups. But the job is very hard and workers get little money for it. Joanne must look at bad pictures and videos, like accidents and fighting. Stacy checks TikTok videos. She sees scary things. Workers feel very sad. Some workers cannot sleep because of bad dreams. Some companies give help, but it is not enough. Experts say that these workers need better pay and good work conditions . Workers are joining together to ask for better conditions. They want more money and help from experts. If things do not change, more people will have problems. But big companies will make a lot of money. Difficult words: sort (to put things in groups), scary (making people afraid), condition (the state that something or someone is in). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has stopped giving food to Zamzam camp in Sudan because the fighting has become worse. This camp, which is in the Darfur region, is home to around 500,000 refugees. The UN has warned that many people could die from hunger. The war in Sudan started in April 2023 due to a conflict between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary group Rapid Support Forces (RSF). In recent weeks, the fighting near Zamzam has become so intense that aid workers had to leave for their safety. Markets have burned, and people are struggling to survive. Sudan is now facing the world’s worst hunger crisis. Half the population, about 25 million people, don’t know when they will eat again. Delivering food is difficult because of bad roads, many military checkpoints , and continuous attacks. The WFP is asking the international community to help by ensuring a pause in fighting so people can get some food. Difficult words: paramilitary (unofficial force organized similarly to a military force), checkpoint (a place where people are stopped and vehicles are examined). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) stopped giving food to the Zamzam camp in Sudan. The war in the country is getting worse, and it is too dangerous for workers to stay. Zamzam camp is in the Darfur region and has 500,000 refugees . The UN says many people there could die from hunger. The war started in April 2023 because the Sudanese army and a group called the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) were fighting for power. In recent weeks, the area around Zamzam become very dangerous. People burn down shops, and there is little food. Half of Sudan’s people, about 25 million, don’t know when they will eat again. Roads are bad, and soldiers check everything. The WFP asks the world to help, so food can arrive soon. Difficult words: refugee (a person who runs away from their country because it is not safe to stay there), recent (happening not long ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) stops giving food to the Zamzam camp in Sudan. The camp is in Darfur. It has 500,000 people. The war is getting worse. It is not safe for workers to stay. Many people have no food. The UN says they can die. The war starts in April 2023. The Sudanese army is fighting with a group called RSF. The fighting near Zamzam is very bad. Shops are burned . People cannot buy anything. They are hungry. Many people in Sudan, 25 million, do not have food. It is hard to bring food because the roads are bad. Soldiers stop cars. The WFP asks the world to help, so food can come soon. Difficult words: camp (a place where people stay for some time, usually in tents), burned (destroyed by fire), soldier (a person who works in the army). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pokémon Day is celebrated every year on February 27th to mark the release of the original Pokémon games. Fans around the world still love the franchise, which has been popular for 29 years. At the Pokémon International Championships in London and a Pokémon Center in Singapore, fans shared why they are still engaged. Many grew up with the games, anime , and trading cards and now pass their love for Pokémon to their children. The Pokémon Company’s CEO, Tsunekazu Ishihara, spoke about the future of Pokémon, its legal dispute with Palworld, and the fate of Ash Ketchum. Esports Director Chris Brown explained that Pokémon’s success is due to its focus on friendship and community. Pokémon is one of Japan’s biggest brands, with valuable trading cards and official merchandise . Some fans believe Ash is now living a quiet life, while others imagine him still on adventures. No matter what happens to Pokémon in the future, its dedicated fanbase ensures its lasting popularity. Difficult words: anime (a style of Japanese film and television animation), dispute (a disagreement or argument), merchandise (products related to a brand, such as toys and clothing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Pokémon Day happens every year on February 27th to remember the first Pokémon games. After 29 years, fans still love Pokémon. At the Pokémon International Championships in London and a Pokémon store in Singapore, fans talked about why they enjoy it. Many started playing as children and now share Pokémon with their kids. The CEO of Pokémon, Tsunekazu Ishihara, spoke about Pokémon’s future, a lawsuit with another game, and what happened to Ash Ketchum. Esports Director Chris Brown said Pokémon stays popular because it brings people together. Pokémon is one of Japan’s biggest brands, with valuable trading cards and many products. Some fans think Ash is relaxing, while others believe he is still traveling. Even after many years, Pokémon is still important to its fans. Difficult words: CEO (the boss of a company), a lawsuit (a legal problem between two companies or people), valuable (worth a lot of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Pokémon Day is on February 27th. It celebrates the first Pokémon games. People still love Pokémon after 29 years. Fans go to a big event in London and a store in Singapore. They talk about why Pokémon is fun. Many play the games as children. Now, they share them with their kids. The boss of Pokémon talks about the future. He also speaks about Ash Ketchum. Some fans think Ash is resting, and others think he is still traveling. Pokémon is very famous. People buy cards, toys, and games. Fans love Pokémon, and they will not stop. Difficult words: celebrate (to take part in a special enjoyable activity), fan (a person who likes and supports a person, sport, sports team, and so on), share (to have or use something at the same time as someone else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 1,000 musicians, including Annie Lennox and Kate Bush, have released a silent album to protest against changes to UK copyright law. The new rules would allow AI companies to use copyrighted content without permission unless the creators opt-out . Musicians fear this would damage their careers, as AI-generated music could replace real artists. The silent album has 12 tracks with only studio noise, symbolizing what music could become if AI companies take control. Ed Newton-Rex, the founder of Fairly Trained, says the government is handing over artists’ work for free, which is unfair. He argues that current UK copyright law already protects musicians, so there is no need for a change. Similar concerns exist in the US, where many lawsuits challenge the use of copyrighted material. Musicians and creative industries are united in their opposition, urging the UK government to enforce existing laws rather than favoring AI companies. Difficult words: copyrighted (protected by law so others cannot copy), opt-out (to choose not to participate in something), symbolize (to represent an idea or meaning). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many famous musicians, like Annie Lennox and Kate Bush, are protesting against new UK copyright rules. They made a silent album with 12 tracks that only have studio noise. This is to show how music could disappear if AI companies use artists’ work without permission . The new rules would let AI companies use songs from the internet unless artists say no. Musicians worry that AI-generated music will replace them and take their jobs. Ed Newton-Rex, the organizer of the protest, believes the government is giving away artists’ work for free. He says that the current copyright law is good enough, and there is no need to change it. Musicians in the US also have problems with AI using their work. Many people want the UK to keep protecting artists. Difficult words: copyright (the legal right to publish, print, or record artistic or musical material), silent (not making any sound), permission (officially allowing someone to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many musicians, like Annie Lennox and Kate Bush, do not like the UK’s new copyright rules . They make an album with 12 tracks. But there is no sound on the album. The album only has noise from the studio. The artists want to show that AI can take music from real musicians. The new rules will let AI companies use songs from the internet. Musicians think this is bad. AI music may take their jobs. Ed Newton-Rex makes the album. He says the government is giving artists’ work to AI for free . He thinks the rules should stay the same. In the US, musicians also have problems with AI. Many people want to keep music safe for real artists. Difficult words: copyright (a law which keeps music, books, and art safe), rule (an official instruction about what people can do), for free (without having to pay any money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On February 28, 2025, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with US President Donald Trump at the White House to discuss a minerals agreement. The deal would have allowed the US to access Ukraine’s rare earth minerals, which are important for economic and strategic reasons. However, the meeting became tense when Zelenskyy warned Trump about trusting Russian President Vladimir Putin, reminding him that Russia had broken agreements before. Vice President JD Vance accused Zelenskyy of disrespect, and Trump ended the meeting suddenly. After this, Trump said he would review US military aid to Ukraine, suggesting that Ukraine was not acting gratefully. Many European leaders showed support for Ukraine, saying Russia was the aggressor . French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Olaf Scholz confirmed their commitment to helping Ukraine. Despite the disagreement, Zelenskyy hoped to repair relations with the US and continue negotiations. This event showed growing tensions between the US and Ukraine. Difficult words: strategic (important for a long-term plan), aggressor (a person or country that attacks another first), commitment (a promise to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On February 28, 2025, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US President Donald Trump in Washington, D.C. They wanted to agree on a minerals deal that would allow the US to get Ukraine’s rare earth minerals. But the meeting didn’t go well. Zelenskyy warned Trump not to trust Russian President Vladimir Putin because Russia broke promises before. Trump’s Vice President JD Vance said Zelenskyy was not respectful , and Trump stopped the meeting. Later, Trump said he would check if Ukraine should still get US military aid . Some European leaders supported Ukraine and said Russia was the problem. The French and German leaders promised to help Ukraine. Even after the argument, Zelenskyy hoped to talk with the US again. Difficult words: rare (not common, unusual), respectful (showing respect), aid (help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On February 28, 2025, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets US President Donald Trump. They talk about a deal for minerals from Ukraine. But the meeting is bad. Zelenskyy tells Trump not to trust Russian President Vladimir Putin. He says that Russia does not keep promises . Trump’s Vice President JD Vance gets angry. Trump stops the meeting. Later, Trump says that he will think about helping Ukraine. Some leaders from Europe say they will help Ukraine. The French and German leaders say that Ukraine needs help. Even though the meeting does not go well, Zelenskyy wants to be friends with the US again. Difficult words: trust (to believe someone), promise (to tell someone that you will certainly do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gene Hackman, a legendary actor who won two Oscars in his 60-year career, was found dead at his home in Santa Fe, New Mexico, along with his wife, Betsy Arakawa, and one of their dogs. Authorities stated that there were no signs of foul play, but the cause of death remains unknown. A maintenance worker discovered the bodies on Wednesday afternoon, finding the front door open. While there was no evidence of forced entry or gas leaks, officials have applied for a search warrant to investigate further. The sheriff mentioned that Hackman and Arakawa had likely been deceased for some time, though it is unclear for how long. The couple lived a quiet life away from Hollywood since Hackman retired in 2004. Tributes from fellow actors and directors have started to appear, honoring Hackman’s contribution to cinema. With the Oscars approaching, many expect a special tribute to be included in the ceremony’s In Memoriam section. Difficult words: foul (wrong or evil), search warrant (a legal document that authorizes an official to enter and search a place), deceased (dead). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Gene Hackman, a famous actor who won two Oscars, died at home with his wife, Betsy Arakawa, and one of their dogs. A worker found the bodies on Wednesday in their house in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He found the front door open but saw no signs of a break-in or gas leak. The police don’t think someone hurt them, but they still look into what happened. Hackman was 95 years old, and he retired in 2004. He and his wife lived a quiet life after he left Hollywood. People from the film industry shared messages to remember him. The upcoming Oscars may include a special moment to honor his life and career. Difficult words: break-in (getting into a place illegally), upcoming (happening soon), honor (to regard someone with respect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Famous American actor Gene Hackman dies. His wife, Betsy Arakawa, and one of their dogs also die. A worker finds the bodies at home in Santa Fe, New Mexico, on Wednesday. The police do not know why they die. But they do not think someone hurt them. The door is open when the worker comes. But nothing is broken . Hackman is 95 years old. He plays in many movies and wins two Oscars. He stops making movies in 2004 and lives a quiet life with his wife. Many people are sad. They remember his great work in films. There may be a special moment to remember Hackman at the Oscars soon. Difficult words: broken (not working, damaged), remember (to bring an image or idea from the part into the mind). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The war in Ukraine began when Russian forces invaded from multiple directions, expecting a quick victory. However, it has now entered its fourth year, bringing devastating consequences for both countries and the world. The World Economic Forum estimates that 2.8 trillion dollars will be lost globally. Ukraine alone will need over 500 billion dollars to rebuild. Food and fuel prices have risen due to disrupted exports and reduced Russian gas supplies. The human cost has been enormous. The UN reports that 122,000 Ukrainian civilians have died, and 3.7 million are displaced. Around 45,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed, with 390,000 injured. Russia has suffered over 750,000 casualties , including up to 172,000 deaths. Military losses include thousands of tanks, aircraft, and naval vessels. Russia now controls 20% of Ukraine, including valuable mineral resources, but many occupied cities are heavily damaged. Meanwhile, most Ukrainian cities, despite continuous missile and drone attacks, remain functional. The war has reshaped global politics and economies, with no clear end in sight. Difficult words: consequence (a result or effect, usually unwelcome or unpleasant), disrupted (stopped or changed something so it no longer works normally), casualty (a person killed or injured in a war or accident). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Three years ago, Russia invaded Ukraine, thinking the war would be quick. But now, both countries and the world are suffering . The war has cost the global economy 2.8 trillion dollars. Ukraine needs over 500 billion dollars to rebuild . Food prices increased, and Europe pays more for gas because Russia is selling less. The UN says Russia killed 122,000 Ukrainian civilians , and 3.7 million had to leave their homes. About 45,000 Ukrainian soldiers died, and 390,000 were hurt. Russia lost over 750,000 soldiers, with up to 172,000 dead. Thousands of tanks, planes, and ships were also destroyed. Russia now controls 20% of Ukraine, but many cities there are badly damaged. Ukrainian cities still suffer attacks but continue to work. The war is not over yet. Difficult words: suffer (to go through something bad or unpleasant), rebuild (to build again), civilian (a person who doesn’t work for the police or army). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Russia attacked Ukraine three years ago. Russia hopes to win quickly. But the war takes longer than everybody thinks. The world loses a lot of money. Food and gas prices are higher. Ukraine needs a lot of money to repair its cities. Many people die. The UN says 122,000 Ukrainian people die. 3.7 million people have to leave home. About 45,000 Ukrainian soldiers die, and 390,000 are hurt. Many Russian soldiers die, too. Tanks, planes, and ships are destroyed . Russia controls 20% of Ukraine. But many places there are broken . Russia still attacks Ukrainian cities. But they keep working. The war is not over yet. Difficult words: repair (to make something work again), destroyed (completely broken or ruined), broken (damaged, not working well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Once France’s largest slave-trading port, now, Nantes acknowledges its past with a memorial. The Memorial to the Abolition of Slavery displays 2,000 boards featuring ship names and trade records, reminding visitors of the city’s deep involvement in the transatlantic slave trade. The Château des Ducs de Bretagne museum further documents this history with plantation registers, shipping logs, and personal testimonies. In the 18th century, Nantes was a leading European hub for slave trade, deporting over 500,000 people. It later became the first French city involved in illegal slavery. A notable exhibit is a 1770 watercolor of the Marie-Séraphique, illustrating the harsh conditions enslaved people endured. Other artifacts include shackles and ceramics. The memorial also encourages reflection on racism and tolerance. Some residents worry that history is being forgotten. Nantes chooses not to erase its past but to educate people about it. The city now seeks to honor those affected and ensure their stories are remembered. Difficult words: acknowledge (to accept or recognize something as true), hub (the center of an activity), artifact (a historical object made by humans), shackle (a part of a chain used to fasten a prisoner’s wrist or ankles together). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nantes was once France’s biggest slave -trading port. Today, it remembers this past with a large memorial. T he Memorial to the Abolition of Slavery shows 2,000 ship names and trade records. The city’s museum also displays plantation records, ship logs, and personal stories. In the 18th century, Nantes deported over 500,000 enslaved people. Later, it was also part of illegal slavery. A famous painting, Marie-Séraphique, shows how captives lived on ships. Visitors can see many historical objects there. The memorial teaches people about racism and tolerance. Some worry that people forget history. Nantes decided not to remove its past but to explain it. Through museums and public discussions, the city hopes to help people learn from history. Difficult words: slave (a person who must work and is not free), enslaved (becoming a slave), captive (a person who cannot move or act and move freely). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nantes is an important port in France. Many years ago, ships from Nantes take people from Africa and sell them as slaves . Today, the city remembers this with a special memorial . It shows ship names and trade records . The museum also has old documents, paintings, and objects from that time. In the 18th century, Nantes sends more than 500,000 slaves people to other countries. A painting called Marie-Séraphique shows how they live on ships. Visitors also see chains and other objects from this activity. The city wants people to learn about racism and history. Some people forget the past, but Nantes chooses to explain it. Now, it helps people understand and remember. Difficult words: slave (a person who is not free and must work for someone else), memorial (a place or object which helps people remember something important), record (information about the past). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nasser Al-Khori leads Generation Amazing, a foundation created as part of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 legacy. He believes sport has the power to transform lives, especially for marginalized children. His team organizes programs that teach young people important life skills, not just football techniques. They also provide psychosocial support to children affected by war and conflict. One of their key projects in Doha helps Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza. Estonia has a large Russian-speaking minority that previously studied in Russian. However, after Russia invaded Ukraine, the government introduced a reform to make Estonian the only language of instruction. Schools had been moving towards this change for decades, but political concerns and Russian influence delayed full implementation . Now, Russian-speaking students, like eight-year-old Victoria, are learning all subjects in Estonian. While some have support at home, many struggle because their families don’t speak Estonian. This is especially challenging in areas where Russian is dominant . The reform aims to improve education equality, as Russian-speaking students previously performed worse than their Estonian-speaking peers . Estonia ranks among the top in global education, but differences remain between urban, rural, and Russian-language schools. The goal is to give all students equal opportunities, including access to Estonian universities. Despite the difficulties, Victoria is determined to succeed in Estonian, knowing it will help her future. Difficult words: implementation (putting a plan into action), dominant (strongest or most common), peer (a person of the same age, status, or ability). Sydney Harbor, one of the busiest waterways in Australia, is home to thousands of boats, including ferries, yachts, and commercial vessels. However, boats use fuel, and global shipping is responsible for 3% of carbon emissions. While Sydney’s commuter ferries will be replaced with electric ones in the next decade, a local startup is already working on solutions to reduce pollution. Their robot, PBot, removes biofouling , a layer of slime that forms on boats and increases fuel consumption by up to 25%. By cleaning it regularly, the company helps ships move more efficiently and reduces emissions. Additionally, it aims to replace toxic antifouling paint, one of the largest sources of ocean microplastics. The startup has also developed CBot, a robot designed to control sea urchins , which are harming marine ecosystems. It creates 3D models of the ocean floor, helping scientists study underwater habitats. These robots make cleaning the ocean easier, showing that technology can play a key role in protecting the environment. Difficult words: biofouling (slime that grows on boats and slows them down), antifouling (a paint that stops the growth of marine organisms on a ship’s bottom noun), urchin (a small sea creature that has a round shell and sharp needle-like points). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

According to the Wall Street Journal, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating UnitedHealth’s Medicare billing practices. The probe focuses on how the company records diagnoses to receive extra payments for Medicare Advantage plans. UnitedHealth claims it is unaware of the investigation and denies wrongdoing. Following the news, UnitedHealth’s shares dropped 7.3%, affecting the broader stock market, while other insurers like Humana and CVS also saw declines. The DOJ has an ongoing lawsuit against UnitedHealth over Medicare Advantage and recently attempted to block its 3.3 billion dollar purchase of Amedisys. Analysts say the investigation creates uncertainty for investors. Some believe the sharp drop in UnitedHealth’s stock price may be an overreaction , as only 15% of its insurance members are in Medicare Advantage. Meanwhile, the company is also offering buyouts to employees in its benefits unit. Lawmakers and regulators continue to scrutinize UnitedHealth’s business practices, particularly its role in rising healthcare costs. Difficult words: probe (investigation), overreaction (reacting extremely), scrutinize (to examine closely). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Almost 200 Venezuelan migrants who had entered the US were deported and have now returned to Venezuela. They had been detained at the US facility in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. Human rights groups claim that they were denied legal assistance, but Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro insists that his government secured their release. The deportation process involved a complex transfer. A US plane flew them to Honduras, where a Venezuelan state airline completed the journey. This marks the second US deportation of Venezuelans in a month. The US government claims that some deportees belonged to a Venezuelan criminal gang, but Venezuela denies this accusation. The first group of returnees was checked, and officials found no gang members among them. Those without pending criminal charges will be allowed to go home. The deportations reflect changing US-Venezuela relations, which had previously been tense under Trump’s administration but now appear more transactional . The future of Venezuelans still in the US remains uncertain. Difficult words: deportee (a person sent to their country by force), returnee (a person who returns to a place, especially after a prolonged absence), transactional (focused on exchanging things for mutual benefit). Have you ever wondered where all the snow goes after a big winter storm? In Montreal, there are ten snow dump sites, each capable of holding the equivalent of 800 Olympic swimming pools. One of the largest sites, the Angrignon dump, is now a massive 30-meter-high snow mountain after a record snowfall. On average, five trucks per minute unload snow, and the city is using 130% more trucks than usual because they fill up so quickly. After the storm, this site alone will contain six million cubic meters of snow, half of what Montreal receives in winter. Despite this, officials are not concerned. The snow mountain will take until September to melt, even with machines helping to reduce its height. No matter how much snow falls, the city continues its operations as usual, ensuring that streets and sidewalks remain clear throughout winter. Difficult words: capable (having the ability or quality to do or achieve a specified thing), equivalent (equal in value or amount). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Iranian judiciary claims they entered the country pretending to be tourists while gathering intelligence. The couple was traveling around the world by motorbike and had planned to stay in Iran for just five days. The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Iran, warning that British nationals face a high risk of being arrested or detained. Despite this, the Foremans went ahead with their journey. Their family is distressed and is working with the Foreign Office to bring them home safely. Cases like theirs vary widely, with some detainees being released quickly while others spend years in detention. A group of insect enthusiasts had the rare opportunity to visit the Northern Territory’s largest insect collection, located at the Berrimah Farm Science Precinct. This collection, managed by entomologist Brian Thistleton, contains 56,000 insects carefully preserved and cataloged. Visitors saw a wide variety of specimens, including butterflies, stick insects, and spiders. The event was part of the collection’s 40th-anniversary celebration and was attended by members of the NT Field Naturalists’ Club, a group of citizen scientists who contribute to insect research. These enthusiasts play a crucial role in detecting new species and biosecurity threats. In 2023, one of them identified the arrival of the papaya mealybug in the region. Dr. Thistleton and his team monitor the club’s Facebook group, where members share their findings. He emphasized that every specimen in the collection is a verified scientific record, helping researchers manage agricultural and environmental threats. For visitors, the experience was an exciting chance to deepen their knowledge. Difficult words: enthusiast (a person who is very interested in a particular activity or subject), entomologist (a person who studies or is an expert on insects), biosecurity (protection against harmful biological threats). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
